title: What If All Synthetic Fertilizer Vanished Overnight?

scenes.text: What if all synthetic fertilizer vanished tonight? Almost half of humanity eats because of it.
In 1908, German chemist Fritz Haber found how to pull nitrogen out of the air and make ammonia.
Carl Bosch scaled it up to factories. Plants need nitrogen, and that is now the main thing fertilizer supplies.
One estimate says the world's harvests would fall to roughly half of today's levels without it.
Researchers estimate that fertilizer made about 48 percent of the world's population possible by 2008.
Farmers could rotate crops and spread manure, but that cannot feed four billion people. The air we breathe is feeding us.
